summary: Rubella virus vaccine live is a lyophilized preparation of the Wistar Institute RA 27/3 strain of live attenuated rubella virus (propagated in WI-38 human diploid lung fibroblasts), used for active immunization against rubella (German measles) in persons 12 months of age and older. It is given as a single 0.5 mL subcutaneous dose, each dose containing not less than 1,000 TCID50 of rubella virus, and induces hemagglutination-inhibition antibodies in 97% or more of susceptible recipients with long-lasting immunity. As a live vaccine it is CONTRAINDICATED in pregnancy (avoid pregnancy for 3 months afterward), in immunosuppression/immunodeficiency, and in certain blood dyscrasias and malignancies. It must not be given intravenously, and immune globulin should not be given concurrently because it can blunt the immune response. (Rubella protection is most commonly delivered as the combined MMR vaccine.)

moa: The vaccine contains live attenuated rubella virus (RA 27/3 strain). After subcutaneous administration, the attenuated virus replicates to a limited extent and stimulates the recipient's adaptive immune system to produce neutralizing and hemagglutination-inhibition antibodies and cell-mediated immunity against wild-type rubella virus, providing durable protection without causing clinical rubella disease.

preg: Rubella vaccine is contraindicated during pregnancy because of the theoretical risk of fetal infection from the live attenuated virus, and pregnancy should be avoided for 3 months following vaccination. Notably, in surveillance of women inadvertently vaccinated shortly before or after conception, abnormalities consistent with congenital rubella syndrome were not observed - so inadvertent vaccination is not in itself an indication for pregnancy termination.
lact: Vaccine virus may be secreted in human milk and transmitted to the infant; mild rubella-like illness has been reported in nursing infants without severe disease. The vaccine should be used cautiously in nursing mothers, though the CDC considers administration of live virus vaccines compatible with breastfeeding.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is described for renal impairment; general immunization principles and contraindications (e.g., immunosuppression) apply.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is described for hepatic impairment; general immunization principles and contraindications apply.

Mild fever, rash, swollen glands, or temporary joint aches can occur, especially in adult women, and usually settle on their own

Seek urgent care for difficulty breathing, swelling, severe rash, or unusual bruising/bleeding after the shot

pearls: Live attenuated RA 27/3 rubella vaccine; single 0.5 mL SUBCUTANEOUS dose (never IV) for persons >=12 months
CONTRAINDICATED in pregnancy (avoid pregnancy for 3 months after) and in immunosuppression/immunodeficiency, blood dyscrasias, and active febrile illness
Do not give immune globulin or blood products concurrently - they blunt the immune response
Arthralgia/arthritis after vaccination is more common in postpubertal women
Biologic/vaccine monograph based on the FDA insert (Meruvax II); rubella protection is most often delivered as the combined MMR vaccine
missed: If a scheduled dose is missed (e.g., the second MMR-containing dose), administer it at the next opportunity per the national immunization schedule - the series does not need to be restarted. There is no daily dosing.
overdose: Overdose is not a clinically relevant concern for a single-dose vaccine. Inadvertent administration of more than one dose is generally well tolerated; manage any reaction symptomatically and report per pharmacovigilance procedures.
